content:
Let the 6 pines be points on a circle with center \(O\). Take \(O\) as the origin.

For any triangle with vertices at position vectors \(u,v,w\) on this circle, its orthocenter has position vector
\[
u+v+w.
\]
Indeed, the circumcenter is \(O\), and the orthocenter vector is the sum of the vertex vectors.

Now split the 6 points into any two triples with position vectors
\[
a,b,c \quad\text{and}\quad d,e,f.
\]
Their orthocenters are
\[
H_1=a+b+c,\qquad H_2=d+e+f.
\]
The midpoint of the segment joining them is
\[
\frac{H_1+H_2}{2}
=
\frac{a+b+c+d+e+f}{2}.
\]
This is independent of how the 6 points are divided into two triples.

Therefore, the treasure is always at the same point, so one dive is enough.

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
